questions.question: The fulfillment process is often called:

options.A: "Procure to pay"
options.B: "Plan to produce"
options.C: "Record to report"
options.D: "Order to cash" (or "inquiry to cash")

questions.explanation: It starts with a customer inquiry (or PO) and ends with the receipt of payment.

questions.question: What is a customer inquiry?

options.A: A legally binding offer by the company to deliver products on specified terms
options.B: A request for product or service information (availability, delivery dates, pricing) without any obligation to purchase
options.C: An internal document that tracks the progress of the fulfillment process
options.D: A request to the customer for payment for the shipped products

questions.explanation: The company responds with a sales quote.

questions.question: What is a sales quote?

options.A: A request from the customer for availability and price
options.B: An approval to purchase requested materials sent to a vendor
options.C: A document authorizing employees to prepare a shipment
options.D: A legally binding offer by the company to deliver certain products or services on specified terms, normally valid for a limited time

questions.explanation: After the time expires, the company must generate a new quote.

questions.question: How does a customer purchase order link two organizations?

options.A: It links the procurement process of the customer to the fulfillment process of the vendor
options.B: It links the fulfillment process of the customer to the production process of the vendor
options.C: It links the financial accounting of both organizations
options.D: It links the cost centers of both organizations

questions.explanation: In Chapter 4 GBI was the customer; in Chapter 5 GBI is the vendor.

questions.question: What is a sales order?

options.A: A request to the customer for payment
options.B: A document sent to the customer with product prices
options.C: An internal document created from the customer PO that the company uses to track progress of the fulfillment process
options.D: An approval to buy materials from a vendor

questions.explanation: It contains quantities, delivery dates, prices, material characteristics and the delivering plant.

questions.question: Which two key tasks does the system perform when a sales order is created?

options.A: Availability check and material reservation
options.B: Goods issue and invoice creation
options.C: Picking and packing
options.D: Credit posting and payment clearing

questions.explanation: If materials are available, they are reserved for the order and not allocated to other orders.

questions.question: What does the availability check determine?

options.A: Whether the customer is creditworthy
options.B: Whether the price is within the tolerance limit
options.C: Whether the necessary materials will be available in time to meet the customer's delivery requirements
options.D: Whether the invoice matches the goods issue

questions.explanation: It is performed for each item in the sales order.

questions.question: What does the shipping step include?

options.A: Creating the invoice, recording payment and closing the order
options.B: Creating a purchase requisition and a purchase order
options.C: Planning production and confirming the production order
options.D: Creating an outbound delivery, picking and packing the materials, and recording a goods issue

questions.explanation: More sophisticated processes include transportation planning.

questions.question: What does an outbound delivery document do?

options.A: Requests payment from the customer
options.B: Authorizes an employee to prepare the shipment
options.C: Records the removal of materials from inventory
options.D: Reserves materials for the sales order

questions.explanation: Picking removes materials from storage locations; packing prepares them for transport.

questions.question: What does transportation planning involve?

options.A: Selecting the vendor and negotiating the purchasing terms
options.B: Determining the pricing procedure and condition types
options.C: Selecting the shipping mode and company, determining the shipping schedule and addressing special requirements
options.D: Selecting the storage location and valuation class

questions.explanation: It is a more sophisticated step beyond the basic fulfillment process.

questions.question: When does the goods issue occur and what does it record?

options.A: When the shipment leaves the plant; it records the removal of materials from inventory
options.B: When the customer pays; it records the clearing of the customer account
options.C: When the sales order is created; it records the reservation of materials
options.D: When the invoice is created; it records the revenue

questions.explanation: It also marks the sales order as ready to be invoiced.

questions.question: Which tasks does the system perform automatically at goods issue?

options.A: Updates the customer master and creates the sales quote
options.B: Creates the purchase order and posts the vendor invoice
options.C: Updates G/L accounts, updates inventory quantity and value, creates FI/CO/material documents and marks the order ready to be invoiced
options.D: Settles the internal order and posts the revenue

questions.explanation: Billing follows goods issue.

questions.question: In which situation is billing integrated with the sales order and payment required before shipping?

options.A: Online retail sales
options.B: Standard wholesale orders
options.C: Return orders
options.D: Rush orders

questions.explanation: Billing documents are usually created after the materials are shipped.

questions.question: Which three steps of the fulfillment process have a financial accounting consequence?

options.A: Customer inquiry, sales quote and sales order
options.B: Sales order, goods issue and billing
options.C: Picking, packing and goods issue
options.D: Goods issue, billing and customer payment

questions.explanation: Inquiry, quote and sales order do not post to the general ledger.

topics.topicName: Enterprise structure: sales organization, channel, division, sales area & shipping point

questions.question: Which enterprise structure elements specific to fulfillment are discussed in the chapter?

options.A: Purchasing organization, purchasing group, plant and storage location
options.B: Sales organization, distribution channel, distribution chain, division, sales area and shipping point
options.C: Controlling area, cost center, profit center and internal order
options.D: Company code, chart of accounts and fiscal year variant

questions.explanation: Client, company code, delivering plant and storage location are also relevant.

questions.question: How do companies typically use a sales organization?

options.A: To group products with similar characteristics into product lines
options.B: To define the path by which products reach customers
options.C: To define the physical location from which deliveries are sent
options.D: To segregate their market based on geography so different sales strategies can be used in different markets

questions.explanation: GBI divides its market into US East, US West, DE North and DE South.

questions.question: What is the relationship between sales organizations and company codes?

options.A: A sales organization can be assigned to several company codes
options.B: A company code can have several sales organizations, but a sales organization is assigned to only one company code
options.C: Each company code has exactly one sales organization
options.D: Sales organizations are not assigned to company codes

questions.explanation: Sales organization UE00 is assigned to company code US00.

questions.question: What is the highest level of aggregation for sales reports?

options.A: The distribution channel
options.B: The division
options.C: The sales organization
options.D: The shipping point

questions.explanation: Each item in a sales document is associated with a sales organization.

questions.question: What does a distribution channel define?

options.A: The path by which an organization gets its products and services to its customers (e.g., wholesale, internet)
options.B: The geographic market segment the company sells to
options.C: The product line a company sells
options.D: The place from which outbound deliveries leave

questions.explanation: GBI has two channels: wholesale (WH) and internet (IN).

questions.question: At which level are distribution channels (and divisions) defined?

options.A: The company code level
options.B: The sales organization level
options.C: The client level, so they can be used across the client
options.D: The plant level

questions.explanation: This is unusual compared with most enterprise structure elements.

questions.question: Distribution channels can be assigned to:

options.A: One or more sales organizations, and the same channel can serve several sales organizations
options.B: Only one sales organization
options.C: Only plants
options.D: Only company codes

questions.explanation: In GBI, US East and DE South sell only through the wholesale channel.

questions.question: To which category in a sales document do all line items of the same document belong?

options.A: Different distribution channels for each line item
options.B: The same distribution channel (and the same sales area)
options.C: Different sales organizations for each line item
options.D: Different company codes for each line item

questions.explanation: All line items in a sales document belong to the same distribution channel.

questions.question: What is a distribution chain?

options.A: A combination of a sales organization, distribution channel and division
options.B: A combination of a plant and a storage location
options.C: A combination of a division and a shipping point
options.D: A combination of a sales organization and a distribution channel that reflects how a sales organization distributes its products

questions.explanation: GBI has six distribution chains.

questions.question: What is the purpose of assigning distribution chains to plants?

options.A: It permits purchase orders to be created for the plant
options.B: It defines the valuation level of the plant
options.C: It permits outbound deliveries from the plant, defining it as a delivering plant
options.D: It assigns the plant to a company code

questions.explanation: The relationship between distribution chains and plants is many-to-many.

questions.question: What is a division used for?

options.A: To group together products with similar characteristics; each division is a product line
options.B: To segregate the market based on geography
options.C: To define how products reach customers
options.D: To group storage locations within a plant

questions.explanation: GBI has divisions accessories (AS) and bicycles (BI).

questions.question: To which element are divisions assigned?

options.A: Plants
options.B: Distribution channels
options.C: Sales organizations
options.D: Company codes

questions.explanation: Divisions, like distribution channels, are defined at the client level.

questions.question: What is a sales area?

options.A: A combination of one sales organization, one distribution channel and one division
options.B: A combination of a sales organization and a distribution channel
options.C: A combination of a plant and a shipping point
options.D: A combination of a company code and a plant

questions.explanation: Example: UE00 + WH + AS.

questions.question: Why can a sales area belong to only one company code?

options.A: Because a division is assigned to exactly one plant
options.B: Because a distribution channel is defined at company code level
options.C: Because sales areas are defined at plant level
options.D: Because a sales organization is assigned to exactly one company code

questions.explanation: All sales documents are associated with a single sales area.

questions.question: Must sales areas be created for every possible combination of sales organization, distribution channel and division?

options.A: Yes, all combinations must exist
options.B: No, only for combinations required to support the organization's strategy
options.C: No, only for the combinations with the wholesale channel
options.D: Yes, but only for company code US00

questions.explanation: E.g., if GBI sells no bicycles via the internet, UW00+IN+BI is not required.

questions.question: What is a shipping point?

options.A: A storage area within a plant where materials are stored
options.B: A facility where a company executes its operations
options.C: A unit that negotiates sales contracts
options.D: A physical location within a delivering plant from which outbound deliveries are sent out

questions.explanation: Examples: a railhead, a port or a designated location in a plant.

questions.question: From how many shipping points can one outbound delivery be shipped?

options.A: Two
options.B: Only one
options.C: Any number
options.D: One per material

questions.explanation: Each outbound delivery is processed from a single shipping point.

questions.question: For what is an express shipping point typically used?

options.A: Rush orders or situations where the customer picks up the shipment
options.B: Routine deliveries
options.C: Return deliveries only
options.D: Deliveries between plants

questions.explanation: The normal shipping point is for routine deliveries.

questions.question: What are loading points (loading bays)?

options.A: Mandatory subdivisions of a plant for storing finished products
options.B: Locations from which purchase orders are sent
options.C: Optional subdivisions of a shipping point that let companies load shipments in parallel or handle special materials
options.D: Areas where invoices are printed

questions.explanation: GBI has no loading points because products have similar characteristics and volumes are low.

questions.question: Which two key factors does the shipping point determination procedure consider (together with the plant)?

options.A: Shipping condition and loading group
options.B: Distribution channel and division
options.C: Condition type and access sequence
options.D: Checking group and checking rule

questions.explanation: The procedure specifies a shipping point for each combination of shipping condition, loading group and plant.

questions.question: What do shipping conditions specify?

options.A: The method used for loading or handling a material
options.B: The path by which products reach the customers
options.C: The conditions under which the company sends the shipment to the customer (Standard, Pick up, Immediately, Returns)
options.D: The terms that determine which party pays for freight

questions.explanation: A shipping condition is assigned to the customer master at the sales area level.

questions.question: What is the shipping condition "Returns" used for?

options.A: To record a return of a shipment from the customer (no shipment is sent)
options.B: To send urgent shipments immediately
options.C: To let customers pick up the shipment
options.D: To ship the order on the standard schedule

questions.explanation: Standard = normal procedure; Immediately = urgent; Pick up = customer collects.

questions.question: What is a loading group?

options.A: A grouping of customers with the same shipping condition
options.B: A grouping of plants with the same valuation group code
options.C: A grouping of shipping points within a plant
options.D: A grouping of materials with the same loading requirements (equipment, time, loading point)

questions.explanation: The loading group is included in the material master.

questions.question: How is the net price in a sales order calculated?

options.A: By multiplying the moving average price by the quantity
options.B: By adding or subtracting charges based on the applicable condition types
options.C: By using the purchase price from the vendor
options.D: By using the standard price of the material only

questions.explanation: Each condition is represented in the system using condition types.

questions.question: What is a condition type?

options.A: A table of parameters used to define condition records
options.B: A procedure that sequences the evaluation of condition types
options.C: A record holding the specific value for a condition
options.D: An element of price determination representing a price, discount, surcharge or freight (e.g., PR00, SKTO, KF00)

questions.explanation: PR00 determines the gross price and SKTO a cash discount.

questions.question: Which condition type determines the gross price of a material?

options.A: SKTO
options.B: PR00
options.C: KF00
options.D: RA00

questions.explanation: SKTO is evaluated for the cash discount; KF00 is freight.

questions.question: What is a condition record?

options.A: A record holding the specific values (e.g., a price of $50) for a condition type for a combination of parameters
options.B: A list of fields available for defining conditions
options.C: The order in which condition records are searched
options.D: A procedure that lists the condition types in a pricing calculation

questions.explanation: PR00 records are defined per material; KF00 records per incoterm.

questions.question: For which parameter is the freight condition record (KF00) defined in the example?

options.A: Material, for a sales organization and channel
options.B: Customer, for a plant
options.C: Incoterms, for a sales area
options.D: Price list, for a document currency

questions.explanation: No freight charge applies for FOB; a UPS shipment costs $9 per kilogram.

questions.question: What do condition tables define?

options.A: The order in which condition records are searched
options.B: The sequence of condition types in a calculation
options.C: The parameters (fields) used to define condition records, e.g., sales organization, distribution channel and material
options.D: The values of price and freight

questions.explanation: Condition table 004 uses sales organization, distribution channel and material.

questions.question: What does an access sequence specify?

options.A: The order in which the system evaluates condition records of each condition type, prioritizing specific over general records
options.B: The condition types that can be used in pricing
options.C: The fields used to define condition records
options.D: The account to which revenue is posted

questions.explanation: Example: tables 005, 006, then 004 for PR00.

questions.question: In the access sequence for PR00 (tables 005, 006, 004), what does the system do first?

options.A: Searches table 004 first because it is the most general
options.B: Uses the pricing procedure to enter the price manually
options.C: Searches for a condition record based on table 005; if none exists, it tries 006 then 004
options.D: Terminates the pricing and displays an error

questions.explanation: Table 005 includes customer and material, so it is the most specific.

questions.question: What does a pricing procedure identify?

options.A: The condition types that can be included in calculating the net price and the sequence in which they are evaluated
options.B: The order in which condition records are evaluated for each condition type
options.C: The parameters used to define condition records
options.D: The values of the condition types

questions.explanation: It also indicates whether a condition type can be entered manually and whether it is required.

questions.question: Which condition type is required in the simple pricing procedure PR0000?

options.A: All five condition types
options.B: RA00 and RB00
options.C: SKTO only
options.D: PR00 only

questions.explanation: If the system cannot determine a value for PR00, the user can enter it manually.

questions.question: What happens if no condition record is found for a REQUIRED condition type?

options.A: The system continues with the next condition type
options.B: The system terminates the price determination procedure and displays an error
options.C: The system uses the price from the material master
options.D: The system creates a new condition record

questions.explanation: If it is not required, the system proceeds to the next condition type.

questions.question: Which parameters are used to select the pricing procedure?

options.A: Plant, shipping condition and loading group
options.B: Material, price list and document currency
options.C: Sales organization, plant and company code
options.D: Sales area, document pricing procedure and customer pricing procedure

questions.explanation: GBI uses RVAJUS for U.S. sales areas and RVAA01 for German sales areas.

questions.question: Which pricing procedure is assigned to all sales areas in the GBI U.S. company code?

options.A: RVAA01
options.B: RVAJUS
options.D: RB00

questions.explanation: RVAA01 is for the German company code.

questions.question: Which two parameters determine the procedure for the availability check?

options.A: Scope of check and replenishment lead time
options.B: Checking rule and checking group
options.C: Shipping condition and loading group
options.D: Condition type and access sequence

questions.explanation: The scope of check is then defined for the combination of checking group and checking rule.

questions.question: What does a checking rule identify?

options.A: The level of detail included in the availability check
options.B: Which data the system considers during the check
options.C: The time required to procure or produce a material
options.D: The process step in which the availability check must be completed (e.g., sales order, outbound delivery)

questions.explanation: Rules exist for the standard SD order and variations such as make-to-stock and consignment.

questions.question: What does a checking group determine?

options.A: The process step in which the check is made
options.B: The level of detail of the availability check (daily or individual requirements)
options.C: The scope of data considered in the check
options.D: The replenishment lead time of the material

questions.explanation: It is assigned to each material in the material master.

questions.question: What does the "daily requirements" option do?

options.A: Evaluates each requirement separately
options.B: Totals requirements for a week only
options.C: Totals all requirements for a material for a day and evaluates availability for them in a single step
options.D: Skips the check for requirements of the same day

questions.explanation: Individual requirements evaluate each requirement separately.

questions.question: In the fulfillment process, what is a requirement?

options.A: Each item in a sales order
options.B: Each purchase order for the material
options.C: Each production order for the material
options.D: Each customer in the system

questions.explanation: A requirement is a general term indicating a need for material.

questions.question: What does the scope of check specify?

options.A: The process step where the check is completed
options.B: Whether requirements are totaled daily or individually
options.C: Which data (stock, inward and outward movements, replenishment lead time) the system considers when evaluating availability
options.D: The shipping point from which the delivery is made

questions.explanation: It is defined for a combination of checking group and checking rule.

questions.question: Which of the following steps result in an inward movement (increase in stock)?

options.A: Purchase orders and production orders
options.B: Material reservations and sales orders
options.C: Outbound deliveries and goods issues
options.D: Customer invoices and payments

questions.explanation: Material reservations and sales orders represent outward movement.

questions.question: What is replenishment lead time (RLT)?

options.A: The time required to ship a material to the customer
options.B: The time required to procure or produce a material
options.C: The time between invoice and payment
options.D: The time a material stays in storage

questions.explanation: RLT is relevant only when materials are not currently available.

questions.question: With "check without RLT", what happens when the materials are not currently available?

options.A: The system assumes materials can be procured and confirms the order
options.B: The system proposes a later date based on RLT
options.C: The system creates a purchase requisition automatically
options.D: The availability check fails and a delivery proposal is not possible

questions.explanation: Message: "Dely proposal: not possible".

questions.question: The scope of check includes RLT, materials are unavailable and the requested date is BEFORE the end of the lead time. What does the system do?

options.A: Confirms the sales order for the requested date
options.B: Rejects the sales order and closes it
options.C: Proposes an alternate delivery date based on the RLT
options.D: Creates a production order

questions.explanation: Example: requested March 3, material available March 4, proposal March 4.

questions.question: The scope of check includes RLT and the requested delivery date falls BEYOND the RLT. What does the system do?

options.A: Assumes the materials can be obtained in time and confirms the sales order
options.B: Proposes an alternate delivery date
options.C: Displays an error and blocks the order
options.D: Reserves the stock immediately

questions.explanation: The availability check then confirms the order quantity.

questions.question: Selling 50 units of a material (MAP $60) at $100 each: what is posted to the inventory account at goods issue?

options.A: A credit of $3,000 (50 x $60), with the offsetting debit to cost of goods sold
options.B: A debit of $3,000 with the offsetting credit to revenue
options.C: A credit of $5,000 (50 x $100)
options.D: A debit of $5,000 to accounts receivable

questions.explanation: Goods issue is valued at MAP; 150 units remain valued at $9,000.

questions.question: In the same scenario, what is posted when the customer invoice is created?

options.A: A credit of $3,000 to inventory and a debit to cost of goods sold
options.B: A debit of $5,000 to the bank account
options.C: A credit of $5,000 to revenue and a debit to the customer account (A/R updated)
options.D: A debit of $5,000 to revenue and a credit to inventory

questions.explanation: Invoice and payment steps do not affect the material master valuation.

questions.question: When the customer payment is posted, which accounts are affected?

options.A: The customer and A/R accounts are cleared with credit postings and the bank account is debited
options.B: The customer account is debited and the bank account is credited
options.C: The inventory account is credited and COGS is debited
options.D: The revenue account is credited and the customer account is debited

questions.explanation: The bank account is provided by the user when the payment is recorded.

questions.question: After the goods issue of 50 of 200 units at MAP $60, what is the MAP?

options.D: $60 (unchanged)

questions.explanation: MAP is recalculated only at goods receipt and invoice receipt.

questions.question: Which three accounts need specific account determination rules in the fulfillment scenario?

options.A: Customer subledger, A/R reconciliation and bank accounts
options.B: Inventory account, cost of goods sold account and revenue account
options.C: GR/IR, price difference and tax accounts
options.D: Inventory, GR/IR and small difference accounts

questions.explanation: The customer subledger account comes from the sales order, the A/R reconciliation account from the customer master.

questions.question: Which posting key is used for the stock outward movement (credit to inventory) at goods issue?
questions.explanation: Posting key 89 is used for stock inward movement at goods receipt.

questions.question: Which posting key is used for the stock inward movement (debit to inventory) at goods receipt?
questions.explanation: Goods receipt increases stock; goods issue decreases it.

questions.question: Which three parameters determine the offsetting entry for an inventory posting?

options.A: Valuation modifier, valuation class and general modifier
options.B: Sales organization, distribution channel and division
options.C: Condition type, access sequence and pricing procedure
options.D: Plant, storage location and shipping point

questions.explanation: The general modifier determines the reason for the inventory posting.

questions.question: Which general modifier applies to the goods issue for a sales order (offsetting entry to COGS)?

options.A: BSA
options.B: VBR
options.C: VAX
options.D: WRX

questions.explanation: BSA is the initial entry of stock; VBR is withdrawal for consumption.

questions.question: Which general modifier applies to the initial entry of stock, and what is the offsetting account?

options.A: VAX; cost of goods sold
options.B: VBR; material consumption expense
options.C: BSA; an inventory suspense account
options.D: DIF; small difference account

questions.explanation: It is used when a company first implements an ERP system and records existing inventory.

questions.question: Which general modifier applies to withdrawal of materials for consumption (e.g., prizes at a trade show)?

options.A: VBR
options.B: VAX
options.C: BSA
options.D: BSX

questions.explanation: The offsetting entry is a material consumption expense account that differs by material type.

questions.question: Why is revenue account determination more complex than the other procedures?

options.A: Because it uses a single parameter that changes with every posting
options.B: Because it does not use account keys or condition types
options.C: Revenue can come from several processes, can have a controlling impact with profitability accounting, and can differ by sales organization, material type and customer type
options.D: Because it applies only to the fulfillment process

questions.explanation: Parameters include application, condition type, sales organization, account assignment groups and account key.

questions.question: In revenue account determination, what does the "application" parameter identify?

options.A: The process that generates the revenue (e.g., V = Sales/Distribution)
options.B: The type of customer
options.C: The type of material
options.D: The type of revenue such as freight or discount

questions.explanation: Customer service (RW – warranty) is another application.

questions.question: What does the account key in revenue account determination identify?

options.A: The type of customer, domestic or foreign
options.B: The type of material, trading goods or finished products
options.C: The sales organization of the order
options.D: The type of revenue (sales, service, freight) and revenue deductions such as discounts

questions.explanation: Revenues go to account 600000 and deductions to the sales discount account 610000 in GBI.

questions.question: When several revenue determination rules conflict, which does the system select?

options.A: The most general rule
options.B: The most specific rule (table 001 is the most specific; tables 004 and 005 the least)
options.C: The rule with the lowest account number
options.D: The rule most recently created

questions.explanation: The system prefers specific data over general data.

topics.topicName: Customer account groups & sales document types

questions.question: What do customer account groups define?

options.A: Groups of materials with the same loading requirements
options.B: Groups of fields on transaction screens
options.C: Categories of customers with similar characteristics; they determine the status of the fields in the customer master
options.D: Groups of plants assigned to a distribution chain

questions.explanation: They also determine number ranges and one-time customer status.

questions.question: In the example, the corporate headquarters that places an order for bicycles is the:

options.A: Sold-to-party
options.B: Ship-to-party (goods recipient)
options.C: Bill-to-party
options.D: Payer

questions.explanation: Retail stores receiving the shipment are ship-to-parties; the outsourced payer makes payment.

questions.question: Which customer role receives the shipment of goods?

options.A: Sold-to-party
options.B: Bill-to-party
options.C: Ship-to-party (goods recipient)
options.D: Payer

questions.explanation: The invoice may be sent to the bill-to-party for verification.

questions.question: Which customer roles require billing and payment data?

options.A: Ship-to-party only
options.B: Bill-to-party and payer
options.C: Sold-to-party and ship-to-party
options.D: No role requires them

questions.explanation: Billing and payment data are not required for the ship-to-party.

questions.question: What is a one-time customer account group used for?

options.A: To store the complete master data of all customers permanently
options.B: To group customers of the same sales area
options.C: To block customers who exceed their credit limit
options.D: As a template (reference customer): data such as name and address are entered when the sales document is created

questions.explanation: It avoids using storage for customers an organization sells to only once or rarely.

questions.question: What is the only required field in the field group account management of the customer master example?

options.A: The payment terms
options.B: The reconciliation account number
options.C: The incoterms
options.D: The delivery priority

questions.explanation: Customer account group field status is similar to G/L account field status.

questions.question: Why are different sales document types needed?

options.A: Because the system allows only one order type per sales area
options.B: Because document types determine the chart of accounts
options.C: Because each order type uses a different company code
options.D: Variations such as rush orders, cash sales, returns and complaints require different data and process steps

questions.explanation: Sales document types specify parameters that determine how the system completes process steps.

questions.question: Which statement about the document types is correct?

options.A: Cash sales always involve accounts receivable, and returns include a goods issue
options.B: Rush orders always use the standard shipping point
options.C: Cash sales do not involve accounts receivable, and returns include a goods receipt rather than a goods issue
options.D: Returns do not create any financial accounting consequence

questions.explanation: Rush orders may be sent from a different shipping point.

questions.question: Which delivery type does a standard order use?

options.A: LF (normal outbound delivery)
options.B: LR (return delivery)
options.C: BV (cash sales)
options.D: F2 (standard invoice)

questions.explanation: A return order uses LR and a cash sale BV.

questions.question: Which delivery type is associated with a return order?

options.A: LF
options.B: BV
options.C: LR
options.D: F2

questions.explanation: Returns reverse the consequences of the previous outbound delivery.

questions.question: What does a delivery block do?

options.A: Prevents a user from completing the delivery (shipping) of an order, e.g., when a credit limit is exceeded
options.B: Prevents a user from creating the sales order
options.C: Prevents the customer from paying the invoice
options.D: Prevents the availability check from running

questions.explanation: The block can be removed when the condition (e.g., credit limit) has been met.

questions.question: Where is the shipping condition preferred if it is defined in both the customer master and the sales document type?

options.A: The customer master
options.B: The material master
options.C: The sales document type (the more specific data)
options.D: The shipping point

questions.explanation: In a conflict, the system uses the more specific data.

questions.question: Which billing type is the standard invoice for a sales order?

options.A: F2
options.B: LF
options.C: BV
options.D: PR00

questions.explanation: A quotation may use a pro-forma invoice, which is not a true invoice.

questions.question: What is a pro-forma invoice?

options.A: A final invoice that clears the customer account
options.B: A credit memo for returned goods
options.C: A document that authorizes shipment
options.D: A representation of the actual invoice if the customer places an order based on the quotation (not a true invoice)

questions.explanation: The cash sales order type uses the "cash sales" invoice.

questions.question: What does the incompletion procedure of a sales document type determine?

options.A: Which condition types are used for pricing
options.B: Which fields the system checks when a document is created and in which process step they are checked
options.C: Which shipping point is used for the delivery
options.D: Which account receives the revenue posting

questions.explanation: A warning about missing data appears only if the warning parameter is selected.

questions.question: In the example, incoterms are missing in the sales order. What happens when an outbound delivery is created?

options.A: Nothing, because incoterms are checked only at order creation
options.B: A warning only, because incoterms are optional
options.C: The order is deleted
options.D: An error results because incoterms are checked in several subsequent steps

questions.explanation: The PO number is relevant only at creation, so a missing PO number does not block later steps.

questions.question: What does the pricing date of a sales document type affect?

options.A: The date on which the goods are shipped
options.B: Which prices and discounts are valid, since prices can be valid for different dates or periods
options.C: The date on which the customer must pay
options.D: The date on which the sales order expires

questions.explanation: The system uses the proposed pricing date in the price determination procedures.

questions.question: Which master data are required to support the fulfillment process?

options.A: Vendor master, purchasing info records and material master
options.B: Cost elements, cost centers and activity types
options.C: G/L accounts, chart of accounts and posting keys
options.D: Material master, customer master, condition records and customer-material info records

questions.explanation: Condition records were discussed in the price determination section.

questions.question: Which additional material master views are relevant for fulfillment?

options.A: Purchasing data and storage data
options.B: General sales data and plant-related sales data
options.C: Work-scheduling data and costing data
options.D: Basic data and vendor data

questions.explanation: Basic data and accounting data are relevant for fulfillment as well.

questions.question: For which organizational level are general sales data of the material master defined?

options.A: A plant
options.B: A company code
options.C: A storage location
options.D: A distribution chain (sales organization + distribution channel)

questions.explanation: To sell material RHMT1000 in UW00 it must be defined for UW00+WH.

questions.question: The delivering plant is specified in the distribution chain and in the material master. Which does the system select?

options.A: The plant in the material master (the more specific data)
options.B: The plant in the distribution chain
options.C: The plant in the customer master
options.D: The plant in the sales document type

questions.explanation: Multiple delivering plants may be specified for a distribution chain.

questions.question: Which parameters appear in the sales plant data of the material master?

options.A: Condition type, access sequence and pricing procedure
options.B: Shipping condition, delivery priority and delivering plant
options.C: Checking group, loading group and transportation group
options.D: Valuation class, price control and valuation group code

questions.explanation: The transportation group groups materials with similar transportation requirements and is used to determine routes.

questions.question: Which three categories of data does the customer master include?

options.A: General data, sales data and accounting data
options.B: General data, purchasing data and accounting data
options.C: Basic data, storage data and sales data
options.D: Sales data, billing data and shipping data

questions.explanation: General data are at client level, accounting data at company code level and sales data per sales area.

questions.question: At which level are the sales data of the customer master defined?

options.A: For each plant
options.B: For each company code
options.C: For each sales area in which the customer does business with the company
options.D: For each distribution channel only

questions.explanation: Sales data are on tabs: general (sales), shipping, billing and partner functions.

questions.question: Which accounting data does the customer master include?

options.A: Delivery priority, shipping conditions and delivering plant
options.B: Incoterms and account assignment group
options.C: Customer pricing procedure and partner functions
options.D: Reconciliation account, payment terms and tolerance group

questions.explanation: In the GBI example the A/R reconciliation account is 110000 and the A/P reconciliation account is 300000.

questions.question: What does the delivery priority in the customer master provide?

options.A: The percentage discount for each customer
options.B: Options for the system to give preference to one customer's order over another
options.C: The tolerance for under deliveries
options.D: The shipping point for each customer

questions.explanation: Other shipping parameters: shipping conditions, delivering plant, partial deliveries and tolerances.

questions.question: Which billing parameter of the customer master is an essential element of price determination?

options.A: Account assignment group
options.B: Delivery priority
options.C: Incoterms
options.D: Partner functions

questions.explanation: Incoterms are used in the freight condition records; the account assignment group is used in revenue account determination.

questions.question: Which four partner functions (roles) must be identified in every customer master?

options.A: Sold-to-party, bill-to-party, ship-to-party and payer
options.B: Sold-to-party, vendor, plant and payer
options.C: Customer, vendor, bank and tax authority
options.D: Sales organization, channel, division and plant

questions.explanation: In the example customer 2000 serves all four roles.

questions.question: What is the key difference between tolerances in fulfillment and in procurement?

options.A: In fulfillment they involve prices only; in procurement quantities only
options.B: Fulfillment does not use tolerances
options.C: In fulfillment they involve under/over deliveries to the customer; in procurement they involve deliveries from a vendor
options.D: Procurement tolerances are in the customer master

questions.explanation: The concepts are otherwise identical.

questions.question: What is a customer-material info record?

options.A: A master data record with data specific to one customer and one material; it is preferred over the customer and material master data
options.B: A master data record with data specific to one vendor and one material
options.C: A record of all sales orders placed by a customer
options.D: A record of the condition types used for pricing a material

questions.explanation: Example: a different delivering plant (DL00 vs. MI00), a higher delivery priority and no partial deliveries for customer 2000 and material RHMT1000.

questions.question: How can the customer-material info record handle the customer’s own material number (e.g., X1000)?

options.A: The system rejects any PO with a material number that differs from its own
options.B: The customer number is replaced by the plant number on the PO
options.C: The material number must be entered manually in the sales order
options.D: The customer can use its own number on its PO, and the system references the info record to identify the material

questions.explanation: The company uses the customer’s number in its sales documents and the info record determines the material.

questions.question: Which testing types and process steps does the chapter list for the fulfillment process?

options.A: Only performance testing of the sales order creation
options.B: Scenario, integration and user acceptance testing of: create sales quote, create sales order, pick/pack/ship, create invoice, receive payment
options.C: Only unit testing of the customer invoice
options.D: Only regression testing after go-live of the shipment

questions.explanation: Various scenarios should use different pricing parameters and sales order types.

questions.question: Which are the five phases of the Lead to Cash process in order?

options.A: Lead to Contact, Contact to Order, Order to Quote, Quote to Cash, Cash to Lead
options.B: Contact to Lead, Lead to Opportunity, Opportunity to Quote, Quote to Order, Order to Cash
options.C: Quote to Lead, Lead to Contact, Contact to Order, Order to Opportunity, Cash to Order
options.D: Opportunity to Lead, Lead to Quote, Quote to Contact, Contact to Cash, Order to Quote

questions.explanation: Each phase is named after the step it comes from and the step it goes to.

questions.question: What does Lead to Cash connect?

options.A: Vendor selection to vendor payment
options.B: Plant maintenance to asset settlement
options.C: Project planning to project settlement
options.D: A customer's interest to buy (SAP Customer Experience) to the realization of revenue in the S/4HANA digital core

questions.explanation: It integrates the front office with the digital core.

questions.question: In which step does a marketing specialist generate leads?

options.A: Lead to Opportunity
options.B: Contact to Lead
options.C: Quote to Order
options.D: Order to Cash

questions.explanation: A lead is created when customer engagement is captured and scored.

questions.question: What happens in the Lead to Opportunity phase?

options.A: The customer is billed for the delivered goods
options.B: The quotation is priced and sent to the customer
options.C: A sales representative decides whether to pursue or drop the lead and converts worthwhile leads into opportunities
options.D: The marketing campaign is created

questions.explanation: Analytics tools can support this decision.

questions.question: What happens in the Order to Cash phase?

options.A: The order is fulfilled, products are delivered or services performed, and the customer is billed
options.B: Marketing generates leads
options.C: The quote is reworked after customer feedback
options.D: The sales representative assesses the opportunity

questions.explanation: The incoming payment closes the process.

questions.question: What does the SAP Analytics Cloud contribute to Lead to Cash?

options.A: It stores all master data of the customer
options.B: It posts the billing document to FI
options.C: It captures real-time KPIs for the whole process from both SAP Sales Cloud and S/4HANA
options.D: It replaces the sales order

questions.explanation: It gives a measurable end-to-end customer experience.

questions.question: When does shipping processing in SD begin?

options.A: When the sales order is saved
options.B: When the delivery document is created
options.C: When the invoice is posted
options.D: When the customer pays

questions.explanation: It copies materials and quantities from the sales order.

questions.question: What does the billing document serve as?

options.A: The proof of a goods movement in inventory
options.B: The request for picking in the warehouse
options.C: The input for the availability check
options.D: The basis for invoices and a data source for FI to monitor and process customer payments

questions.explanation: It copies data from the sales order and the delivery.

questions.question: Which step closes the Sales and Distribution process?

options.A: The goods issue
options.B: The creation of the billing document
options.C: The delivery creation
options.D: The incoming payment, which belongs to Financial Accounting

questions.explanation: Customer payment clears the open receivable.

topics.topicName: TS410 – Organizational levels in Sales & Distribution

questions.question: What does the sales organization represent?

options.A: The enterprise grouped by sales and distribution requirements, i.e., a regional, national or international subdivision of the market
options.B: A means by which customers procure goods
options.C: A group of materials or services
options.D: The physical place where shipping is processed

questions.explanation: It is the highest summation level in sales statistics.

questions.question: How many company codes can a sales organization be assigned to?

options.A: Several company codes at once
options.B: No company code
options.C: Exactly one; but several sales organizations can belong to one company code
options.D: Only the plant, never a company code

questions.explanation: At least one sales organization is needed for order to cash.

questions.question: What is a distribution channel?

options.A: A means by which customers get goods or services, such as wholesale, retail or internet trade
options.B: A grouping of materials such as spare parts
options.C: A responsible unit for shipping
options.D: A unit of external accounting

questions.explanation: At least one is required in SD.

questions.question: What tasks does a distribution channel perform?

options.A: Posts the goods issue and the invoice
options.B: Defines the chart of accounts and fiscal year
options.C: Controls picking and packing
options.D: Defines responsibilities, achieves flexible pricing and differentiates sales statistics

questions.explanation: Several channels can be assigned to one sales organization.

questions.question: How is a sales area defined?

options.A: As a combination of plant, storage location and shipping point
options.B: As a combination of company code, plant and cost center
options.C: As a combination of client, company code and segment
options.D: As a combination of sales organization, distribution channel and division

questions.explanation: Each SD document belongs to exactly one sales area.

questions.question: Which statement about a sales area is true?

options.A: A sales area can belong to several company codes
options.B: The assignment of an SD document to its sales area cannot be changed
options.C: The sales area of a document can be changed anytime
options.D: A document can belong to several sales areas

questions.explanation: A sales area belongs to only one company code.

questions.question: How are delivery plants assigned?

options.A: To a combination of sales organization and distribution channel; one plant can be assigned to several combinations
options.B: To a division only
options.C: To a customer only
options.D: To a storage location only

questions.explanation: Several plants can be assigned to one combination.

questions.question: What is the shipping point?

options.A: A unit that groups materials in a plant
options.B: A unit that sells goods to customers
options.C: The highest-level organizational unit of shipping, responsible for the entire shipping process
options.D: A key for the legal entity that issues invoices

questions.explanation: It can be a loading ramp, a mail depot or a rail depot.

questions.question: How are plants and shipping points related?

options.A: A plant can have only one shipping point
options.B: A shipping point belongs to a sales organization only
options.C: A shipping point can serve only one plant
options.D: One plant can have several shipping points, and one shipping point can be assigned to several plants

questions.explanation: A shipping point is a physical place near the delivering plant.

questions.question: How can a plant be linked to sales organizations?

options.A: A plant can belong to several company codes
options.B: A plant belongs to one company code but can be assigned to several sales organizations that can sell from it
options.C: A plant can be assigned to one sales organization only
options.D: A plant is assigned to a distribution channel only

questions.explanation: Within a company code, several sales organizations can be active.

questions.question: Which levels of the material master are relevant for SD?

options.A: Basic data (client), sales organization data (sales org and distribution channel) and sales: plant data (delivering plant)
options.B: Only the storage location data
options.C: Only the company code data
options.D: Only the purchasing group data

questions.explanation: Basic data is valid for all organizational units in a client.

questions.question: At which level is the customer role data of a business partner maintained?

options.A: At the company code level
options.B: At the plant level
options.C: At the sales area level (sales organization, distribution channel, division)
options.D: At the client level only

questions.explanation: It contains data for orders, deliveries, invoices and customer payments.

questions.question: In which role is the reconciliation account of a customer entered?

options.A: In the FI Customer role, for each company code
options.B: In the general role of the business partner
options.C: In the customer role of the sales area
options.D: In the vendor role of the purchasing organization

questions.explanation: The FI Customer role is relevant for accounting.

questions.question: Why is the name and address stored in the general role of the business partner?

options.A: It is only used in billing documents
options.B: It must be maintained per sales area
options.C: It must be maintained per company code
options.D: It is relevant for both SD and accounting and stored once at client level to avoid redundancy

questions.explanation: It is valid for all organizational units in the client.

questions.question: What does condition master data include?

options.A: Stock quantities and storage bins
options.B: Prices, surcharges, discounts, freights and taxes
options.C: Partner functions and payment terms
options.D: Vendor bank details

questions.explanation: Conditions can depend on, e.g., customer and material pricing group.

questions.question: What does the condition type control in a condition record?

options.A: The company code and the plant
options.B: The shipping point and the route
options.C: The sold-to party and the payer
options.D: The condition class, scales, header or item level relevance and the validity period default

questions.explanation: Examples of classes are price and discount.

questions.question: How is a sales document structured?

options.A: Header and item only
options.B: Header, item and schedule line
options.C: Order, delivery and billing
options.D: Customer, material and plant

questions.explanation: Schedule lines hold delivery quantities and dates.

questions.question: What data is stored in a schedule line?

options.A: Customer and payment data valid for the whole document
options.B: Material and price information for the item
options.C: Partner functions of the document
options.D: Delivery quantities and delivery dates, belonging uniquely to an item

questions.explanation: An item with a follow-up delivery needs at least one schedule line.

questions.question: Which partner functions are mandatory for sales order processing?

options.A: Contact person and forwarding agent
options.B: Sold-to party, ship-to party, payer and bill-to party
options.C: Sales employee and carrier
options.D: Sold-to party and forwarding agent only

questions.explanation: They may be identical or different.

questions.question: What does each mandatory partner function mean?

options.A: Sold-to receives the goods, ship-to pays the invoice, payer places the order, bill-to receives goods
options.B: Sold-to pays, ship-to places the order, payer receives the goods and bill-to ships the goods
options.C: Sold-to places the order, ship-to receives the goods, bill-to receives the invoice and payer pays the invoice
options.D: Sold-to receives the invoice, ship-to places the order, payer receives the goods, bill-to pays

questions.explanation: Partner functions are copied from the customer master as default values.

questions.question: What happens when the address of the ship-to party is changed manually in a sales document?

options.A: The master record is not affected
options.B: The business partner master is updated
options.C: The change is blocked by the system
options.D: All other sales documents are changed

questions.explanation: Partners can also be defined at item level.

questions.question: How does the system find prices, surcharges, discounts, freight and taxes in a sales order?

options.A: By asking the user for every price
options.B: By copying them from the goods issue document
options.C: By automatic pricing using the condition technique, with manual changes possible
options.D: By reading them from the vendor info record

questions.explanation: Output determination also uses the condition technique.

questions.question: At which level is the availability check in sales orders performed?

options.A: At plant level for the corresponding item
options.B: At client level for the document
options.C: At storage bin level for the delivery
options.D: At company code level for the order

questions.explanation: The plant is determined automatically or entered manually.

questions.question: In which sequence does the system determine the delivering plant automatically?

options.A: Material master, ship-to party master, customer-material info record
options.B: Customer-material info record, ship-to party customer master, material master
options.C: Ship-to master, material master, info record
options.D: Sales organization, distribution channel, division

questions.explanation: The first valid default value found is used.

questions.question: What is the incompletion log?

options.A: A log of all changes made in the document
options.B: A list of open items of the customer
options.C: A list of delivery blocks
options.D: A list of fields required for the document or further processing that the user has not filled, shown automatically on saving

questions.explanation: Customizing decides which fields are part of the log.

questions.question: What is output in SD?

options.A: The quantity of goods delivered to the customer
options.B: The posting to the customer receivables account
options.C: Information sent to the customer via media such as mail, EDI or fax, e.g., an order confirmation
options.D: The picking list for the warehouse

questions.explanation: Forms are in SAPscript, Smartform or PDF.

questions.question: Which organizational unit is responsible for creating deliveries?

options.A: The sales organization
options.B: The distribution channel
options.C: The division
options.D: The shipping point

questions.explanation: Each outbound delivery is processed by one shipping point.

questions.question: Why are order items with different shipping points not copied into the same outbound delivery?

options.A: Because they have different divisions
options.B: Because each outbound delivery is processed by exactly one shipping point
options.C: Because they have different payers
options.D: Because they belong to different company codes

questions.explanation: The shipping point cannot be changed in the delivery.

questions.question: Which characteristics must be equal to combine items of different sales orders in one outbound delivery?

options.A: Payer, billing date and destination country
options.B: Division, material group and plant
options.C: Sold-to party, sales area and company code
options.D: Shipping point, due date and ship-to address

questions.explanation: Billing documents combine by payer, billing date and destination country.

questions.question: How is a delivery document structured?

options.A: Header and item, without schedule lines
options.B: Header, item and schedule line
options.C: Header only
options.D: Item and schedule line only

questions.explanation: Each schedule line of the order can become an item in the delivery.

questions.question: What prerequisites must be met before an order can be delivered?

options.A: The invoice has been paid and the billing document posted
options.B: The billing document exists and the payer is known
options.C: A ship-to party, a plant and a shipping point exist, the schedule line has a confirmed quantity and the order is due
options.D: The goods issue is already posted

questions.explanation: Collective processing can create deliveries in the background.

questions.question: What are backorders in SAP S/4HANA?

options.A: Sales orders that cannot be (fully) confirmed by the availability check
options.B: Sales orders that have been fully delivered
options.C: Sales orders that have been canceled by the customer
options.D: Sales orders waiting for payment

questions.explanation: Backorder processing can change existing confirmations.

questions.question: What does a BOP segment contain?

options.A: The collection of all confirmation strategies
options.B: A mass availability check of requirements
options.C: Criteria identifying a set of requirements handled similarly, plus a prioritizer that ranks them
options.D: The warehouse tasks for picking

questions.explanation: The standard availability check works on a first-come, first-served basis.

questions.question: What is a BOP run?

options.A: A single check for one item during order entry
options.B: A report on posted goods issues
options.C: A set of delivery documents created in a batch
options.D: A mass availability check of requirements, e.g., sales order items, based on a BOP variant, run online or in the background

questions.explanation: It is run, e.g., after an MRP run or before a delivery due list.

questions.question: What does the BOP confirmation strategy "Win" mean?

options.A: Requirements lose their confirmation
options.B: Requirements are fully confirmed on the request date; if that is not possible, the run stops with an alert
options.C: Requirements may get a better, equal or worse confirmation
options.D: Requirements only get equal or worse confirmation

questions.explanation: Win has processing priority 2.

questions.question: What does the BOP confirmation strategy "Lose" do?

options.A: Requirements are fully confirmed on the request date
options.B: Requirements keep or improve their confirmation
options.C: Requirements lose their current confirmation, releasing quantity for more important requirements
options.D: Requirements receive an earlier confirmation date

questions.explanation: Lose has processing priority 1.

questions.question: What is the prerequisite for posting goods issue in standard configuration?

options.A: Picking-relevant items are completely picked, i.e., the pick quantity equals the delivery quantity
options.B: The customer invoice has been posted
options.C: The customer has paid the order
options.D: The sales order has been billed

questions.explanation: Warehouse tasks execute the physical picking in EWM.

questions.question: Which actions does the goods issue posting trigger automatically?

options.A: The creation of a purchase requisition and a quotation
options.B: A debit posting to the customer receivables account
options.C: A material document and accounting document reducing inventory, a controlling document, an update of the billing due list and the document flow
options.D: The posting of the incoming payment

questions.explanation: A Material Ledger document is generated too.

questions.question: Which accounting postings does the billing document trigger?

options.A: A debit to the customer receivables account and a credit to the revenue account
options.B: A debit to inventory and a credit to receivables
options.C: A debit to revenue and a credit to the bank account
options.D: A debit to the GR/IR account and a credit to the vendor

questions.explanation: CO-PA and group reporting documents may also be created.

questions.question: What does the document flow provide?

options.A: A list of customers with open items
options.B: A list of all stocks per plant
options.C: A list of all pricing conditions
options.D: A list of linked preceding and subsequent documents showing the history and status of the SD process

questions.explanation: It helps to answer customer questions quickly.

questions.question: What is the purpose of SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM)?

options.A: Managing the posting of customer invoices
options.B: Supporting the physical transportation of goods: requirements, planning, carrier selection, execution and charge calculation
options.C: Planning the production of finished goods
options.D: Maintaining the vendor master data

questions.explanation: It can use sales orders, purchase orders and deliveries as transportation requirements.
